run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T10:57:52Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because frontend-proxy is returning HTTP 504 to requests for the cart/checkout paths after its ~15s upstream timeout. The slow upstream is frontend, whose /api/cart and /api/checkout handlers block on the cart service, and cart is failing every cart-storage call with gRPC FAILED_PRECONDITION 'Can't access cart storage ... Wasn't able to connect to redis' from its ValkeyCartStore. The deepest evidence-backed layer is the redis backend valkey-cart: the otel-collector's redis receiver stopped receiving data from valkey at 10:56:00, at the same time cart's redis commands stopped and its connection errors began (first observed cart log line 10:58:11). The valkey-cart pod itself stayed Running, ready and 0 restarts, with no OOM (memory failcnt 0, peak 5.69MiB of a 10MiB limit) and only 1.5-7.9% CFS throttling, so why the valkey process/endpoint stopped serving is not determined: valkey emitted no readable log lines and no change history is integrated. Impact is observed on frontend-proxy, frontend, cart, checkout and the load-generator client; other services returned no error spans.

claims.text: In the hour to 2026-11-15T11:14:11Z, frontend-proxy had 961.29 STATUS_CODE_ERROR span calls versus 33392.98 STATUS_CODE_UNSET; the same query returned 84.0 error spans for cart, 256.39 for frontend and 13.5 for checkout.

All frontend-proxy error spans in the hour are on span_name "ingress" (961.29); span_name "router frontend egress" has 0 error spans and 17177.14 UNSET, and "ingress" additionally has 16215.84 UNSET spans.

frontend-proxy "ingress" error spans carry http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR" and last ~15.0s (15,000,011-15,001,202 us); the matching load-generator GET/POST client spans also show 504 at ~15s.

Full trace a545ba7815ee3f559a6bbcc06809bf79 shows load-generator user_view_cart 15.003s -> load-generator GET 504 15.003s -> frontend-proxy ingress 504 15.001s -> router frontend egress (error=true, http.status_code=0) 15.001s -> frontend GET 14.999s with http.status_code=200, i.e. the proxy timed out while frontend was still working.

At 11:10:00Z the 10-minute increase of frontend-proxy ingress error spans was 656.03 against 1653.55 non-error ingress spans, i.e. about 1.09 errors/second, numerically matching the alert annotation's current value 1.0888888888888888; the error rate was still non-zero at the last returned point.

The frontend-proxy 5-minute error increase was ~1-3 spans from 10:37 to 10:56, then jumped to 53.3 at the 10:57 point, 170 at 10:58, 393 at 11:00, peaked at 553.3 at 11:02 and was 172.4 at 11:10; the identical series for frontend starts at 10:59 and for cart at 11:00.

cart server spans fail: span POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart had 38.77 STATUS_CODE_ERROR calls and POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 45.23 STATUS_CODE_ERROR calls in the hour, and the failing cart spans last 468-480 seconds with error detail 'Status(StatusCode="FailedPrecondition", Detail="Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() ... GetCartAsync').

The cart container in pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logged the line "Wasn't able to connect to redis" first at 10:58:11.139Z (none in the 10:57:30-10:58:30 window before that) and repeatedly through 11:04:28.538Z, in total 135 matching lines in 10:40-11:14:11.

frontend error spans in the hour are on executing api route (pages) /api/cart 79.34, GET /api/cart 31.53, POST /api/cart 46.31, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 31.53, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 46.31, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 7.12, POST /api/checkout 7.12, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 7.12, with http.status_code 500 and grpc status 9/13.

checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans fail after 373-376 seconds with detail 'cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout: rpc error: code = FailedPrecondition desc = Can't access cart storage ... Wasn't able to connect to redis', and the child checkout->cart GetCart span shows grpc status 9 for the same reason.

cart's redis client spans were still counted before the failure (HGET 6308.93/h, EXPIRE and HMSET 2934.74/h in the hour) but their 5-minute increase falls to 0 from the 11:02:00Z point onward, while cart GetCart/AddItem span rates collapse from ~1078/569 at 10:56 to ~8/15 by 11:10.

In the incident window the otel-collector redis receiver produced redis_memory_used_bytes for valkey that stops changing exactly at 10:56:00Z (constant 1710360 from 10:56 through the last point 11:05) and redis_cpu_time_seconds_total{state="user"} that is likewise frozen at 2.6249 from 10:56:00Z; these series come from job="otel-collector", pod otel-collector-564d9c7987-vpmw7, scope github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/receiver/redisreceiver.

valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr and cart-755465879b-t9mf7 were both Running with ready=true and restartCount 0, started 2026-11-15T10:24:49Z and 10:24:51Z respectively, inside a 21-pod otel-demo set in which no pod showed a restart.
Service valkey-cart exposes port 6379 (ClusterIP) and its Endpoints object lists address 100.96.2.228 on port 6379 with no notReadyAddresses; cart's Endpoints entry is 100.96.2.233:8080.

cart's deployment (generation 1, revision 1) sets env VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, and the valkey-cart deployment (generation 1, revision 1) runs image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine; neither container defines a readinessProbe or livenessProbe.

The valkey-cart container is limited to cpu 10m and memory 10Mi (requests 2m/4Mi), yet its working set stayed at ~3.8-4.1MB, its container_memory_max_usage_bytes never exceeded 5,693,440 bytes, and container_memory_failcnt stayed 0 throughout 10:20-11:14.
valkey-cart's CPU throttling ratio (throttled/CFS periods) stayed between 0.015 and 0.044 through 10:56 and only rose to 0.027-0.079 between 11:00 and 11:07, never approaching saturation.

All five cluster nodes report Ready=True with no MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure or NetworkUnavailable condition, and both kube-dns pods (coredns-b5494cbf4-48phd, coredns-b5494cbf4-z7jj2) are Running with restartCount 0.

During the window the kubelet emitted 'Stopping container cart' for pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s at 11:00:42Z preceded by a Warning FailedKillPod at 11:00:41Z ('failed to KillContainer ... DeadlineExceeded'), and cAdvisor still showed that pod's cart container with a flat 29,138,944-byte working set through the 11:10 point.

No error-status span series was returned for product-catalog, currency, payment, shipping, email or accounting in the hour to 11:14:11Z (currency only STATUS_CODE_OK, product-catalog 17470.10 STATUS_CODE_UNSET), and the sampled product-catalog GetProduct spans complete in 96-143us with rpc.grpc.status_code="0".

Primary explanation: the alert fires because frontend's /api/cart and /api/checkout requests exceed frontend-proxy's ~15s upstream timeout while frontend blocks on cart, and cart returns nothing because its redis backend is unreachable; the proxy records 504 ingress error spans (961/h, ~1.09/s at 11:10), which is the frontend-proxy error signal the alert reports.

Deepest supported layer: the redis backend valkey-cart stopped serving at ~10:56:00Z. Its pod never restarted and stayed low on CPU/memory, yet the otel-collector redis receiver (running on node i-0a709b85c49d987be, a different node from valkey on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae) stopped getting data from it at exactly 10:56:00, cart's redis HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE spans drop to zero from 11:02, and cart's client reports 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' from 10:58:11.

Alternative not distinguished by the evidence: the network path to the valkey-cart pod broke (the Service and its ready endpoint 100.96.2.228:6379 exist and DNS is healthy, so this would have to be a pod-level dataplane/protocol-path problem), rather than the valkey process itself hanging. Without valkey logs or an in-pod connection test these two cannot be separated.

Memory-limit OOM of the valkey container is rejected: its memory limit is 10Mi, but the working set stayed ~3.8-4.1MB, max usage peaked at 5,693,440 bytes, container_memory_failcnt was 0 for the whole window, and the container restarted 0 times.

The termination of the older cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s is not the trigger: its kill events are at 11:00:41-11:00:42Z, while the frontend-proxy error rate already jumped at the 10:57 data point and the surviving cart pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logged its own redis failures from 10:58:11Z.

A cluster- or node-wide infrastructure cause is not supported: all five nodes are Ready with no pressure conditions, CoreDNS is up with 0 restarts, and the otel-demo pods (including cart on the same node as valkey, i-0146cb0d0caf26bae) are all Running with 0 restarts.

Other otel-demo services do not show error spans in the same hour: product-catalog has only STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans (17470.10) with sampled GetProduct calls at 96-143us and rpc.grpc.status_code="0", and currency is STATUS_CODE_OK only; payment, email, shipping and accounting returned no error series.

Investigate valkey-cart directly as the next step: run redis-cli PING/INFO/LATENCY against valkey-cart:6379 from another pod, capture valkey stdout (it produced no readable log lines in this window), and check the Cilium endpoint/datapath health for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr, since the pod itself never restarted.

Review the cart/valkey deployment configuration in change history (not integrated here) for changes to VALKEY_ADDR, the 10m CPU / 10Mi memory limits, and the missing readiness/liveness probes on both containers; add probes and realistic redis limits so a stalled valkey is detected rather than reported ready.

Consider a latency-based timeout budget: frontend cart/checkout calls hang for hundreds of seconds and the proxy turns them into 504 at 15s, so align cart's redis connect/command timeouts and the frontend/checkout gRPC deadlines with the proxy route timeout to fail fast instead of holding requests for 6-8 minutes.

gaps: Why valkey-cart stopped responding at ~10:56:00Z is not determined: the valkey-cart container produced no readable log lines in 10:40-11:14:11, in-pod exec/redis-cli checks are not available in this Run, and change_history is not integrated.

The RequestErrorRate alert rule itself is not loaded in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no_data), so the rule's exact metric, window and threshold could not be verified; the 10-minute frontend-proxy ingress error rate of 656.03/600s = 1.09/s only numerically matches the alert's stated 1.0888888888888888.
Absence of NetworkPolicy in namespace otel-demo is not proven: the networkpolicies query returned zero objects with status no_data, so a policy-based block of cart->valkey cannot be excluded.
No non-Running pod was returned cluster-wide, but that view also came back no_data, so clean pod state outside otel-demo is not proven.

Whether the valkey outage continues at 11:14:11Z is unknown: redis_memory_used_bytes had no data at 11:14:11Z, cart container logging stops at 11:04:28.538Z, and the last Prometheus data point for the proxy error series is 11:10:00Z (still 172 errors per 5m).

Why the older cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s was being deleted is unknown: only Killing/FailedKillPod events were captured for it, its owning ReplicaSet cart-9fd895bb7 is not present in the current ReplicaSet list, and no SuccessfulDelete/SuccessfulCreate event for it was returned.

Jaeger results are a biased sample (e.g. traces_search_by_tags reported 'backend returned as many traces as requested', and a cart trace search for 11:05-11:14:11Z returned no_data), so the full set of affected operations and the exact per-operation error rates during the last minutes are not known.
next_steps: Run redis-cli PING/INFO against valkey-cart:6379 from a pod on another node and from the cart pod, and inspect valkey stdout/stderr and Cilium endpoint state for valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr.
Obtain the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the monitoring repository/Alertmanager config to confirm which frontend-proxy metric, window and threshold produced the value 1.0889.

Review change history for otel-demo cart/valkey deployment manifests around 2026-11-15T10:56Z (VALKEY_ADDR, resource limits, probes, image digests) since the change-history integration is not available in this Run.
Check whether valkey-cart recovered after 11:14Z and whether any automatic rollout or manual restart of valkey-cart occurred after the authorized window.
